blocking.finding: Dependency contradiction on M4.1. The markdown says M4.1 depends on M4.6a 'for glow_pole_w_m2 only' and lists M4.6a, M4.0 and M4.1 as 'all startable NOW' in one parallel wave of 'disjoint files'. The JSON hard-codes M4.1.depends_on = [M4.6a], so M4.1 cannot start until M4.6a is published after an independent physics PASS and pinned. M4.6a also edits sim/ailang.toml, sim/ailang.lock and runtime/cache that M4.1 builds against, so the files are not disjoint, and the two-step ship.ism split is the only thing keeping M4.1 off the critical path of an external publish.
blocking.fix: Make M4.1 depends_on [] in the JSON with 'step 2 (glow_pole_w_m2) after M4.6a' as an explicit sub-step (or put M4.6a in wave 0 and drop the 'startable now/parallel' wording). State that the pin bump lands in its own commit before M4.1 step 2 and that M4.1 step 1 does not touch the toml, lock or cache.

summary: PASS (85/100), with three plan-wording fixes to make before Mark approves. The revised design doc answers all round-1 and round-2 objections. I re-derived the round-trip times (Earth 8.796343, ship 1.240885, t_e 0.043984), the ISM and glow numbers, the drag-ledger ratio 0.9999999999999999, the 19-minute tau_b bound and the lore premises at 1ef3bc9 with my own AILANG probes and greps, and all match. The doc stays inside D-6/D-11/D-12/D-14/D-15/D-16/D-19/D-20/D-21 and leaves canon and infrastructure choices (HB-4 vs 4.32 ly, CI deploy key) to Mark. The round-2 carve-out was legitimate: every present blocker gave a concrete proposed_fix, none disputed direction, and each fix was applied as written. The sprint plan covers all 10 sub-milestones and all 18 ACs with runnable commands, adds no Python, puts the package work (M4.6a) before its use, and is honestly sized against M2. Blocking defects: (B1) M4.1 is hard-dependent on M4.6a in the JSON but 'startable now, glow_pole only' in the markdown, in a wave described as disjoint-file parallel; (B2) AC6 is assigned to M4.4 although its command needs M4.5, which depends on M4.4, so M4.4 cannot pass under rule F4; (B3) S1 'blocks the M4.2/M4.3b/M4.6 merges' but M4.3b depends on M4.2 and S1's renders come from M4.6 in wave 4, with no stated stacking mechanism.
